I'm buying my first house right now. Anyone have tips for a first time home buyer?
Make sure it isn't full of owls. Lousy bastards...
Have a real HVAC guy inspect the heating and air conditioning system. Don't rely on your standard home inspector.
Or bats. Had a colony of bats in my attic. Cost 3k to get rid of them. They weren't there when I bought, the moved in afterwards. That goes to how well sealed your attic is.

EditTo add from the other comments: hire an electrician to inspect the place. If it's an older house, check the attic for burn marks. And this critical, meet the neighbors. Worse then buying a money trap, is being finically fucked surrounded by people you hate. Edit::excuse my grammar mistakes.

Check for the following: sticking doors or windows, cracked drywall/plaster, cracked brick, doors that won't stay open or closed. This can indicate that at best the house is not level, or at worst that you have foundation problems. I was in the market a few years back and found a log cabin I fell in love with until I asked the realtor about some cracked walls upstairs. She said she hadn't noticed it before. My bullshit meter pinged then and there. Any realtor worth a damn at least notices deficiencies beforehand and usually has some answer prepared. After inspecting the floor on the kitchen I saw that the slab was cracked... badly. It wasn't noticeable in the other rooms where hardwood floors were installed. Long story short, the property had a lot of trees, so a lot of shade. The property stayed wet as a result and the house started settling. They hired a crew to level the house and they cracked the fuck out of the slab. I ended up getting a house in a better location and without the headaches the other had.

Speaking of foundations, if the house is on joists as opposed to a slab, consider making a few plumbing modifications to make your future a bit easier. Install shutoff valves very liberally, install cleanout fittings very liberally, get a drain bladder that will fit your drain, get a drain snake. This might seem a bit excessive but it's best not to wait until you have a backed up drain that hinders your lifestyle for possibly days. I don't use chemical cleaners because I have a septic tank but even if you don't have one, many plumbers will refuse to work on it if there's a chance their guy is going to get blasted in the face with Draino if he has to cut a pipe.

Also, buy some pipe insulation and wrap your pipes.

If you are not familiar with the area, ask (neighbors/someone impartial) about flooding/draining in the area.

Buy a couple of books on plumbing and electrical. Consider Taunton's line of books.

That's a few off the top of my head.

Paint before moving in. Your wife is gonna want to put her own touch on every room and this will lead to wanting to change the wall colors. Just spend a weekend getting it done so you don't come home to a disaster when she tries to do it herself in a month.
